summary: Turn the SidekickMenu search box from on-by-default to opt-in: a consumer who renders <SidekickMenu items={items} /> sees no search input, and search appears only when the consumer passes searchEnabled={true}. Existing installations get the hidden default just by upgrading, because the default is resolved in code, not stored anywhere. Enabling search keeps every 1.7.0 search behaviour; no new prop is added. Because the default changes, the release must be a major version with a migration note and the reference docs updated.
roles: Library consumer (developer): installs jattac.libs.web.zest-sidekick-menu and chooses whether the search box appears by passing the existing searchEnabled prop.
End user of a consumer app: sees no search box unless the developer turned it on; gets today's search when it is on.

requirements.text: With no searchEnabled prop, <SidekickMenu items={items} /> renders no search input; the search box exists only when the consumer passes searchEnabled={true}.
requirements.rationale: Most menus are small and do not need search, yet the box currently takes the top slot and grabs focus on open. Making it opt-in keeps the default menu clean and matches the request that existing installations get the hidden behaviour without code changes.
acceptance: Rendering <SidekickMenu items={items} /> produces no element with the placeholder 'Search menu...', and the rest of the menu renders as it does today.
Rendering <SidekickMenu items={items} searchEnabled={true} /> produces the search input; searchEnabled={false} and searchEnabled={undefined} produce none.
Opening a menu without search does not focus a search field and leaves no empty gap where the box used to be.
edgeCases: An app that upgrades without changing its code shows no search box, because the default comes from the component and no browser storage holds a preference.
If search was enabled and a term was typed, then the prop changes to false, the box disappears and the menu is no longer filtered: no invisible search term may keep filtering the list.
A consumer who already passes searchEnabled={false} sees no change from before.
pitfalls: Do not keep a hidden input mounted: a hidden search box must not be reachable by Tab or a screen reader.
Do not gate non-search features (favourites, breadcrumbs, shortcuts, gestures, rail) on searchEnabled.

facts.subject: search box
facts.value: when searchEnabled is absent, false or undefined

requirements.text: Passing searchEnabled={true} gives the consumer the full 1.7.0 search experience: the box shows, typing filters, clearing restores the previous section, searchPlaceholder, searchIcon and searchAutoFocus still apply, and arrow keys and numbered shortcuts act on the filtered list.
requirements.rationale: Only the default state should change. Consumers who opt in must not get a reworked search they did not ask for, so the existing behaviour is the specification.
acceptance: <SidekickMenu items={items} searchEnabled searchPlaceholder="Find pages..." /> shows an input with that placeholder, and typing 'about' filters the list to matching items.
Clearing the term restores the section the user was in before searching, as today.
With searchEnabled={true} and searchAutoFocus={true} the input receives focus when the menu opens; with searchAutoFocus={false} it does not.
edgeCases: With railCollapsible and a collapsed rail, the search box stays hidden even when searchEnabled={true}, and appears again when the rail expands (today's rule, unchanged).
A term with no matches shows the existing empty state; enabling search must not introduce a new one.
The search term is never persisted: a reopened menu starts with an empty term regardless of what was typed before.
pitfalls: Do not change matching fields, matching rules or result ordering while flipping the default.
Do not make enabled search depend on a new global config flag or another prop.

requirements.text: The changed default ships as a major version 2.0.0 with an entry in docs/breaking-changes.md that names searchEnabled, states the new default and shows searchEnabled={true} as the migration.
requirements.rationale: Apps install this package by version range and render whatever the default gives them. A silent change of a default UI behaviour would remove their search box on upgrade without warning; the house rule requires a breaking change to be noted and the version bumped to match.
acceptance: package.json version is 2.0.0 at publish time and the release is tagged v2.0.0.
docs/breaking-changes.md has a v2.0.0 entry naming the searchEnabled default change with the migration snippet <SidekickMenu items={items} searchEnabled={true} />.
The v2.0.0 entry states that no export, prop name or type is removed or renamed by this change.
edgeCases: A consumer who already passes searchEnabled={false} needs no change, and the note says so.
The note says search is otherwise unchanged, so consumers do not expect other surprises in the same release.
pitfalls: Do not ship the default flip in a 1.x release: the version and the note must match the change.
Do not bump the version without the breaking-changes entry, or the two disagree.

requirements.text: Every doc page that presents search as on by default is updated to present it as opt-in: README.md, docs/features.md, docs/examples.md, docs/api.md and docs/configuration.md.
requirements.rationale: Documentation is what consumers read before they upgrade. If the reference pages still say the default is true, the breaking-change note is contradicted by the pages people trust most.
acceptance: docs/api.md shows searchEnabled with default false and describes it as needing true to show the box.
docs/configuration.md shows searchEnabled: false in its defaults snippet, and its section says search is off unless enabled.
docs/examples.md no longer says 'The search feature is enabled by default'; its search recipe passes searchEnabled={true}.
README.md's basic example still works (now without a search box), and its feature list says search must be enabled, with a one-line example.
docs/features.md keeps a working searchEnabled={true} example.
Each edited docs page keeps its previous/next links.
edgeCases: Searching the docs for 'enabled by default', 'searchEnabled' and 'Search menu...' finds no statement that contradicts the new default.
The README's first working example renders a menu with no search box, matching the new default.
pitfalls: Do not document the new default only in breaking-changes.md while api.md or configuration.md still say true.
Do not break the docs' previous/next navigation when adding the v2.0.0 entry.

requirements.text: Tests prove the new default and keep proving the old search behaviour: a test asserts no input is rendered when the prop is omitted, and every existing search test opts in with searchEnabled={true} instead of relying on the old default.
requirements.rationale: This edits code already released, so its already-deployed behaviour must stay proven while the default changes. Without a test on the default itself, it can silently flip back in a later refactor.
acceptance: A test renders <SidekickMenu items={items} /> and asserts the search input is absent; another renders it with searchEnabled={true} and asserts it is present.
The existing search tests in SidekickMenu.test.tsx pass searchEnabled and still pass with their assertions intact.
npm test passes with no search test deleted or skipped.
edgeCases: A test that needs search but forgets searchEnabled fails loudly instead of silently testing nothing; assert the input exists before typing into it.
Tests for autofocus or numbered shortcuts on filtered results enable search, or they no longer exercise the behaviour they name.
pitfalls: Do not delete or skip search tests to make the suite green after the default flips.
Do not 'fix' a failing query by asserting a hidden input: the requirement is that the input is not rendered at all.

outOfScope: A visible toggle, button or '/' shortcut that reveals search at runtime; only the prop turns it on.
A global searchEnabled option on ZestSidekickConfigProvider.
Changing search matching (searchTerms, label matching) or result ordering.
Storing a per-user or per-app preference for search in localStorage or sessionStorage.
Changing the search input's markup, accessible name or styling beyond hiding it by default.

nonFunctional.statement: Hiding the search box must not disturb keyboard use: with default props no invisible control is focusable and opening the menu does not move focus, while with search enabled the input stays keyboard-reachable and behaves as today.
nonFunctional.acceptance: With default props, Tab and the menu's arrow, Escape and numbered-shortcut keys traverse exactly the controls that existed before the search box and never land on an invisible element; with searchEnabled={true} the input can be focused and typed into by keyboard.

nonFunctional.statement: Hiding search adds no work and removes what the box cost: with default props the menu mounts no input, does no non-empty search filtering, and the built bundle does not grow.
nonFunctional.acceptance: With default props the rendered DOM contains no search input and filtering only ever runs with an empty term; npm run build output for dist/index.js and dist/index.esm.js is no larger than v1.7.0's (measure both before and after).

risks: Existing consumers lose the search box on upgrade with no code change; that is the request, but it must be a major release with a clear note or it will look like a bug.
Several docs pages currently claim search is enabled by default, so one missed page leaves the docs contradicting each other.
Existing tests query the search input by placeholder without enabling search, so the suite will go red until they are updated deliberately.
searchAutoFocus still defaults to true; when the input is absent the focus effect must do nothing rather than error or move focus elsewhere.
The README feature list still advertises built-in search, which reads as on-by-default to a new consumer.
glossary: Consumer: a developer whose app installs the published package.
searchEnabled: the existing SidekickMenuProps boolean that renders the search input; no new prop is introduced.
Opt-in: search appears only when the consumer explicitly passes searchEnabled={true}.
Breaking change: an upgrade that changes what existing apps render without the app changing its code.

coverage.note: Library consumers turn search on per menu instance with the existing prop; end users of their apps are the ones who see it.
No records or fields: the change touches one boolean prop default and stores nothing.
No records, ownership or sharing: nothing is protected by this change.
No user-entered data; searchEnabled is a boolean and any value other than true behaves as off.
Hidden is the default with no input and no empty-search state; enabled is today's search. Dropping an active term when search is hidden is my chosen default.
Nothing is created or submitted, so double submits and concurrent edits do not apply.
Menu size and search cost are unchanged; hiding the box only removes work when it is off.
Nothing is deleted and nothing new is stored when the box is hidden.
No personal data is collected, stored or displayed by this change.
No focus or keyboard regression when hidden, search behaviour unchanged when enabled, and no bundle growth; covered by the two non-functional requirements.

assumptions: Search stays controlled only by the existing per-instance searchEnabled prop: no global config-provider switch, no runtime button and no keyboard shortcut to reveal it.
When search is off, any active search term is dropped so the menu is never left filtered by a term the user can no longer see, and no empty-results state is shown while search is hidden.
Enabling search keeps 1.7.0's look and behaviour exactly: default placeholder 'Search menu...', autofocus default true, custom icon, filtering, and numbered shortcuts over the filtered list.
